expected_core_reactions.description: LSS (lanosterol synthase) cyclises 2,3-oxidosqualene to lanosterol, described as one of the earliest steps in sterol biosynthesis and as forming the first tetracyclic sterol skeleton. The paper locates the enzyme in the endoplasmic reticulum.
expected_core_reactions.quote: LSS (Lanosterol synthase) catalyzes one of the earliest steps in sterol biosynthesis by converting 2,3-oxidosqualene to lanosterol, a key intermediate in the production of cholesterol and other sterol compounds
expected_core_reactions.rationale: An explicit catalytic statement with named substrate, named product and named enzyme, placed by the paper inside the requested pathway.

expected_core_reactions.description: CYP51A1 (lanosterol 14alpha-demethylase), a cytochrome P450, converts lanosterol to 4,4-dimethylcholesta-8(9),14,24-trien-3beta-ol by removing the C-14alpha-methyl group. The paper calls this demethylation the initial control point for cholesterol and sterol biosynthesis.
expected_core_reactions.quote: It is a cytochrome P450 enzyme that catalyzes the conversion of lanosterol to 4,4-dimethylcholesta-8(9),14,24-trien-3β-ol
expected_core_reactions.rationale: An explicit catalytic statement with both sides named; it also chains cleanly to R1 through lanosterol, the only string-identical shared metabolite in the paper.

expected_core_reactions.description: MSMO1 (methylsterol monooxygenase 1) carries out the three-step monooxygenation that demethylates 4,4-dimethylsterols and 4alpha-methylsterols, products of which the paper says can subsequently be metabolised to cholesterol.
products: demethylated sterols (not named as a discrete compound in this paper)
expected_core_reactions.quote: It primarily catalyzes the three-step monooxygenation required for the demethylation of 4,4-dimethyl and 4alpha-methylsterols, which can be subsequently metabolized to cholesterol.
expected_core_reactions.rationale: The transformation and its enzyme are stated, but the substrate is given only as a COMPOUND CLASS and no product is named as a discrete molecule, so this reaction cannot be chained to either neighbour on named metabolites.

expected_core_reactions.description: DHCR24 (delta24-cholesterol reductase, also called 3beta-hydroxysterol delta24-reductase) reduces desmosterol to cholesterol. The paper states this is the final step of the cholesterol biosynthesis pathway.
expected_core_reactions.quote: DHCR24 (δ24-cholesterol reductase, also known as 3β-hydroxysterol Δ24-reductase) is an enzyme that catalyzes the final step in the cholesterol biosynthesis pathway (mevalonate pathway), converting desmosterol to cholesterol
expected_core_reactions.rationale: An explicit catalytic statement with both sides named and identified as the terminal step of the requested pathway. NOTE: topologically orphaned in this paper, because no stated reaction produces desmosterol and no reductant is named.

The non-enzymatic members of the quoted enrichment list (SREBF1, SREBF2, LBR) are not part of this stage and are recorded separately.
expected_major_subprocesses.quote: Reactome enrichment analysis of the differentially expressed genes showed that the cholesterol biosynthesis pathway (R-HSA-191273, P -adjust < 0.0001, Fig. 2E ) had the highest degree of enrichment, the enriched genes including FDPS (farnesyl diphosphate synthase, FDPS) , LBR , SREBF1 (sterol regulatory element binding transcription factor 1, SREBF1) , HSD17B7 , MSMO1 , SQLE , MVD (mevalonate diphosphate decarboxylase, MVD) , LSS , EBP , DHCR24 , CYP51A1 , SREBF2(sterol regulatory element binding transcription factor 2 , SREBF2) , FDFT1 , HMGCR (3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-CoA reductase , HMGCR) , HMGCS1 (3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-CoA synthase 1 , HMGCS1) , MVK (mevalonate kinase , MVK) , IDI1 (isopentenyl-diphosphate delta isomerase 1, IDI1) , and ACAT2 (acetyl-CoA acetyltransferase 2, ACAT2)

The paper explicitly assigns ACAT2, HMGCS1, HMGCR, MVK, MVD, IDI1, FDPS, FDFT1 and SQLE to the cholesterol biosynthesis pathway, and separately calls the pathway the mevalonate pathway and singles out HMG-CoA reductase as a key enzyme of it, but it states NO reaction for any of them: no acetyl-CoA, no HMG-CoA, no mevalonate, no isopentenyl diphosphate, no farnesyl diphosphate, no squalene, no substrate and no product anywhere for these enzymes. uncertainties: NAMED VERSUS DETAILED IS THE CENTRAL ISSUE IN THIS PAPER, and S5 is where it is recorded. The paper's own output is transcriptomic: three large enrichment gene lists. Those lists explicitly place ACAT2, HMGCS1, HMGCR, MVK, MVD, IDI1, FDPS, FDFT1, SQLE, NSDHL, EBP, HSD17B7, LBR and LIPA inside the cholesterol biosynthesis or steroid biosynthesis pathway, giving full protein names for many of them, and state NO reaction for any of them. Only four enzymes (LSS, CYP51A1, MSMO1, DHCR24) carry a catalytic statement, and all four of those statements are cited background in the Discussion.

Consequently NO upstream metabolite is named as a FREE COMPOUND anywhere in this paper. Verified by substring census over full_text: the tokens acetyl-CoA (1), mevalonate (3), isopentenyl (1), farnesyl (4), squalene (2) and HMG-CoA (2) occur ONLY inside enzyme names (acetyl-CoA acetyltransferase 2; mevalonate diphosphate decarboxylase; mevalonate kinase; isopentenyl-diphosphate delta isomerase 1; farnesyl diphosphate synthase; farnesyl-diphosphate farnesyltransferase 1; squalene epoxidase; HMG-CoA reductase), plus the phrase (mevalonate pathway) and the substrate 2,3-oxidosqualene. Free squalene, free mevalonate, free HMG-CoA, free acetyl-CoA, isopentenyl diphosphate and farnesyl diphosphate are never named as metabolites. The pathway therefore starts, as far as this paper is concerned, at 2,3-oxidosqualene.

The phrase 'mevalonate pathway' appears exactly once, and this paper uses it as a SYNONYM FOR THE WHOLE CHOLESTEROL BIOSYNTHESIS PATHWAY ('the final step in the cholesterol biosynthesis pathway (mevalonate pathway)'), not as the name of the upstream arm. I used it only as an alias on S5 and flag the loose usage here rather than treating it as the paper's own name for the pre-lanosterol segment.

THE CURATED ROUTE IS NOT CONNECTED END TO END. Only R1 and R2 chain, through the string-identical metabolite lanosterol. R3's substrate is a compound class and its product is unnamed. R4's substrate, desmosterol, is produced by nothing stated in this paper, so it is topologically orphaned. I did not bridge these gaps, and bridging them would require importing the pathway from general knowledge.

R3 (MSMO1) is medium confidence for that reason: the enzyme and the transformation type are stated, but the substrate is only a class ('4,4-dimethyl and 4alpha-methylsterols') and no product compound is named.

NO COFACTOR IS NAMED ANYWHERE for any of the four reactions: no NADPH, no NAD(P)H, no molecular oxygen, no reductant for the DHCR24 reduction. Molecular oxygen is recorded as a secondary participant of R3 only because the word 'monooxygenation' implies it; the paper never names it.
The paper contains a genuine typo, 'lanosterene' (also 'tetra-closterane'), used for lanosterol. It is not a separate compound and must not be minted as one.

DHCR24 appears under four surface forms in this paper: DHCR24, '24-dehydrocholesterol reductase' (gene list), 'delta24-cholesterol reductase' and '3beta-hydroxysterol delta24-reductase'. All collapse to one protein.

DIRECTION CAUTION: this paper reports that the CaSR antagonist UP-regulates these genes and that the resulting cholesterol OVERPRODUCTION is what reduces tumour cell viability. That is the opposite of the usual statin narrative, and an extractor that assumes inhibition would invert the paper's claim.

S6 (SREBP regulation) is transcriptional regulation, carries no reaction ids, and is low confidence, consistent with how I treated the regulatory findings in the other papers of this set. It is marked detailed_in_paper: false because no mechanism is given here.
